notes:
THIS BUILD HAD NO SCRIPTURE IN IT AT ALL. Eight beats, every one white,
every spoken line in the story reported in modern English. Luke 22:54-62 is
almost entirely dialogue, and none of it was being heard.

A WOMAN SPEAKS FIRST, AND SHE WAS IN WHITE. The denial starts because a servant
girl says six words out loud. Lifted verbatim as WOMAN (pink):
  w56  Luke 22:56  'This man was also with him.'
  n1 is trimmed to the frame only and a new n1b carries the retelling.

PETER'S OWN DENIALS, lifted verbatim as SCRIPTURE (light blue -- he is a man in
the story). Two of the three, not all three, so it does not turn into a list:
  s57  Luke 22:57  'Woman, I know him not.'
  s60  Luke 22:60  'Man, I know not what thou sayest.'
  n2 keeps its id and now retells the first and carries the second and third
  denials; n2b retells the last one.

RED ADDED -- the only red in the whole video, and it is a memory. Luke 22:61 has
Peter remembering the exact words Jesus had said to him hours earlier, and a
red-letter KJV inks that remembered sentence:
  jv61 Luke 22:61  'Before the cock crow, thou shalt deny me thrice.'
  n5a is trimmed to the frame and n5a2 carries the retelling. Putting it in red
  is the point of the video -- his voice arriving in Peter's head at the worst
  second of his life.

CONSIDERED, LEFT OUT. Luke 22:58, the second accuser's 'Thou art also of them,'
and Peter's 'Man, I am not' -- left out to keep the middle of the video moving;
the pattern is already clear from the first and third. Luke 22:62, 'And Peter
went out, and wept bitterly,' is Luke writing and could be blue, but n5b already
says it plainly and putting it in Old English there would slow the fall.

NO GREEN: the Father does not speak in Luke 22:54-62.

WHY-LAW: Jesus looked at Peter after Peter had publicly disowned him three times,
and the look was not scorn. Milk: he knew before you failed, and he chose you
anyway.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: After they arrested Jesus, Peter followed at a distance and warmed himself by a fire in the courtyard, trying not to be noticed.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: A servant girl saw his face in the firelight, looked hard at him, and said it out loud.

segments.speaker: woman
segments.text: This man was also with him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: This one was with him too, she said. Not an accusation — just a girl recognizing a face. And Peter answered her.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Woman, I don't know him. A little later, someone else said the same thing. Then a third man, an hour after that, swore he was one of them. And Peter denied it harder every time.

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: Man, I know not what thou sayest.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: I don't know what you're talking about. Three times now, out loud, in front of strangers, he had said he had never met him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And right then, while the words were still in his mouth, a rooster crowed.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Across the courtyard, Jesus turned and looked straight at Peter. Just looked at him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And Peter remembered. Jesus had said this to his face, that very night, and Peter had sworn it would never happen.

segments.speaker: jesus
segments.text: Before the cock crow, thou shalt deny me thrice.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Before the rooster crows, you will say three times that you don't know me. He had told him. And now the rooster had crowed, and Jesus was looking right at him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He went outside and wept bitterly.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But the look wasn't scorn. It was the face of someone who already knew, and already loved him anyway.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He looked at Peter in his worst moment — and still chose him. He looks at you the same way.

stills_wanted.ST2: ST2 now carries the frame, the servant girl's verbatim line, and its retelling. Frame her, not Peter: a young servant girl on the far side of the fire, leaning slightly forward, firelight full on her face, looking directly at someone off to the side of frame. Ordinary and unafraid — she is not accusing anyone, she is recognizing him.
stills_wanted.ST3: ST3 now carries four beats — both of Peter's verbatim denials and both retellings. Frame the denial as distance: Peter half turned away from the fire, palms open and out in front of him, face closed, eyes on the ground rather than on whoever is asking. The warmth of the fire behind him and nothing warm in him.
stills_wanted.ST6: ST6 now carries the frame, Jesus's remembered words, and the retelling. Frame the memory rather than the courtyard: close on Peter's face the instant it lands, mouth still open from the last word he said, the courtyard soft and out of focus behind him. The whole shot is one man realizing what he just did.
